chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Horace Henderson calls again from Indianapolis; Fletcher's arrangements
summary: In late 1930 Horace sought a trumpet and trombone for a band at the Walker Theater in Indianapolis; Jones joined for the music itself, since Horace played Fletcher Henderson arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: October of '30, when we come back. October of 1930. Now, about the latter part, say about the end of December of '30, here's old Horace again. Here he comes again. He's telling me, "Now, I've got a band over here in Indianapolis." He was playing in a place called the Walker Theater there, and he says, "I've got a band in here, but I only have one trumpet and I need a trumpet and trombone," and he says, "Can you find a good trombone," and stuff, you know, and I'm so crazy about the music I'll go back with him again, you know. I want to play so. After he went off and left us in Buffalo and he comes back, drove over from Indianapolis, which is only a little over 100 miles, about 110 miles or something. So he drives over from Indianapolis, and that's
when I said, 'Yeah, I can get you a man.' Because he had the band -- I don't know if you've heard of this band or not. It was called Coris Davis (PHONETIC). Coris Davis, yeah. It was --
Yeah. And he had a band and it was really the Hardy Brothers Band. Did you ever hear of them?

The Hardy Brothers. It was their band. One played sax and the other one plays -- I forget. I think he -- one played saxophone and one played trumpet, yeah, that's right. So there was about seven of them playing in the pit band over there. That's the first time I seen the Ink Spots, you know, on the stage there, in a show. So he took us over there and -- he wanted to know if I could find a trombone player. So I told him yeah. Well, see, I liked the bands because I just liked to play the arrangements they had, you know.
Yeah. You wanted to go on.

Yeah, there were good arrangements back then in them days, too. These guys play arrangements for me, you don't have to talk no money. I'm ready to go and live the best I can, you know. And Horace always played Fletcher's
arrangements, you know. That was it in them days.

Yeah, sure. And sometimes he'd go in the book and take them. Sure, he'd go in the book and take them sometimes, you know. Horace, he had a lot [say] And you could tell that they'd been used already, you know. He'd bring them in, and we were so happy to get them, you know.
